artists.biography:
The Coral are an English band formed  in 1996 in Hoylake on the Wirral Peninsula in England. The band first emerged during the early 2000s (decade)  and found success with their debut album The Coral (2002) and follow up Magic and Medicine (2003). Their self-titled debut album was nominated for the 2002 Mercury Music Prize  and later voted the fourth best album of the year by NME Magazine.

The band continued to record and tour throughout the decade releasing the albums The Invisible Invasion (2005) and Roots & Echoes (2007).

In 2008 guitarist Bill Ryder-Jones left the band, however The Coral continued as a five-piece. Their sixth album Butterfly House was released in 2010.

perplexity.description:
Coral Island is the tenth studio album by English rock band The Coral, released on April 30, 2021, via Run On Records and Modern Sky UK. It marks the band’s first double album and a significant evolution in their sound, embracing a sprawling, psychedelic, and experimental approach. The album is a concept record centered around a fictional coastal town, blending nostalgic British seaside imagery with darker, more surreal themes. Musically, Coral Island fuses the band’s signature melodic rock with elements of folk, psychedelia, and art rock, creating a richly textured and atmospheric listening experience. The lead single, “Faceless Angel,” exemplifies this shift, showcasing moody instrumentation and evocative storytelling.

As The Coral’s first new release since 2018’s Move Through the Dawn, Coral Island stands out for its ambitious scope and narrative depth, reflecting the band’s willingness to explore new creative territory. The album was well-received by critics, with Mojo ranking it seventh on their list of the best 75 albums of 2021. Commercially, it reached number two on the UK Albums Chart and achieved strong showings in Scotland, Germany, and Switzerland. With its imaginative concept and adventurous sound, Coral Island solidified The Coral’s reputation as one of Britain’s most inventive and enduring rock acts.
